text:
Tom: Heads up — Cloudburst POC with NovaHealth. Procurement just asked if we can put the 2-week burst + reserved week on a single PO and they require exec signature on the MSA before issuing the PO. Any major blockers?
Sara (Legal): We received their MSA redlines earlier today — they tightened the DPA subprocessor clause and added a SOC2 addendum ask. Need to review whether their written-consent requirement blocks our prefix/KV caching for POC.
Ajay (Presales): From presales side: we can split billing technically (trial credit + reserved capacity). Quick draft ratecard snippet:
```
trial_credit: 50k tokens
gpu-reserved-p1: $1,200/day
on-demand-gen: $0.45/token
```
If procurement wants a single PO, we usually map to two line items on one PO.
Maria (Finance): Single PO is OK but we need them to include our vendor legal entity address and tax ID on the PO. Also note: single PO covering both trial credit and reserved commit will still need two invoice line items so revenue mapping is correct.
procurement-bot: Automated check — incoming PO missing vendor address and signature block. Recommended template: https://redwood.co/templates/po-template. See section 2.1 for multi-line-item mapping.
Tom: @Sara (Legal) — can you confirm whether we can accept their DPA redline for a limited POC? They say no caching without prior consent which might force us to disable prefix caches. That would change latency/cost assumptions we just quoted.
Sara (Legal): Short answer: not without modification. Their redline forbids automatic caching by default; we can offer a scoped Appendix that limits cache usage to ephemeral, in-memory KV for POC only and excludes long-term subprocessor transfers. We should loop in Security for SOC2 addendum acceptance. If customer insists on exec-sig before PO, legal needs Sales Ops to route countersign quickly.
Ajay (Presales): For quoting purposes if cache must be disabled we should adjust expected token consumption ~+25% and propose increasing trial credit or reducing reserved price. I'll update the estimate and post a revised order form.
Maria (Finance): Please include explicit billing codes on the draft order form. If they provide one PO with two line items we can accept it, but it must include our billing contact and the vendor tax details.
Tom: I'll upload a draft order form in this thread in a minute. @Sara (Legal) — confirm whether we can accept countersign after PO for the POC (low-risk) or whether exec-sig is mandatory ahead of PO. Procurement is pressing on timeline.
Sara (Legal): We can accept countersign after PO for trial-only POCs if Sales Ops flags it as "PO-first" and Security grants temporary approval for cache scope. Otherwise exec-sign required. I'm tagging Security outside this thread.
procurement-bot: PO template link re-post: https://redwood.co/templates/po-template. Also: attach vendor W-9 (US customers) or equivalent.
Tom: Thanks — plan: I will (1) post revised order form with two line items and adjusted numbers if cache disabled, (2) request Sales Ops e-sign routing if exec-sig required, (3) ask Security for SOC2 addendum quick review. Back soon with draft. :thumbsup:
Sara (Legal): Great. If you can, add a short paragraph in the Appendix that limits caching to ephemeral buffers for 14 days for the POC. That should make their legal team more comfortable.
Ajay (Presales): I'll tweak the usage projection and ratecard and attach both to the draft order form.
Maria (Finance): I'll standby to validate invoice mapping once you post the draft.
Tom: Ack — uploading draft now.
